title: United States History: Voices and Perspectives (Student Edition, National Edition)

summary: A middle-school survey of United States history from the first Americans to the present, organised into 18 topics. Each topic opens with an Introduction lesson, works through Learn the Events and Inquiry Activity lessons built on primary sources and multiple perspectives, and closes with a Review and Apply lesson.

toc.label: Front matter
toc.title: Historian's Toolkit
toc.covers: How historians use chronology, sources, geography, economics, and civics as tools of inquiry.

toc.label: Topic 1
toc.title: The First Americans (up to 1492)
toc.covers: Migration into the Americas and the civilisations and cultures of Mesoamerica, South America, and North America before 1492.

toc.label: Topic 2
toc.title: Exploration and Colonization (AD 476-1718)
toc.covers: Changes in Europe that drove exploration, Columbus and the Spanish conquest, the Columbian Exchange, and French, Dutch, and English claims.

toc.label: Topic 3
toc.title: The English Colonies Are Settled and Grow (1607-1754)
toc.covers: Jamestown and the New England, Middle, and Southern colonies, colonial economies, slavery, self-government, and the Great Awakening.

toc.label: Topic 4
toc.title: The American Revolution (1754-1782)
toc.covers: The French and Indian War, British taxes and colonial protest, the Declaration of Independence, and the war for independence.

toc.label: Topic 5
toc.title: First Governments and the Constitution (1777-present)
toc.covers: The Articles of Confederation, the Constitutional Convention and its compromises, ratification, the Bill of Rights, and constitutional principles.

toc.label: Topic 6
toc.title: The Early Republic (1789-1823)
toc.covers: Washington's and Adams's presidencies, the first political parties, Jefferson and the Louisiana Purchase, the War of 1812, and the Monroe Doctrine.

toc.label: Topic 7
toc.title: Political and Geographic Changes (1828-1850)
toc.covers: Jacksonian democracy, Indian Removal, westward expansion and Manifest Destiny, Texas, the Mexican-American War, and the California Gold Rush.

toc.label: Topic 8
toc.title: Life in the North and the South (1820-1860)
toc.covers: Northern industry, transportation, and immigration; the Southern cotton economy and enslaved life; and the reform movements of the era.

toc.label: Topic 9
toc.title: Division and Civil War (1821-1865)
toc.covers: Sectional compromises over slavery, the crises of the 1850s, Lincoln's election and secession, and the Civil War.

toc.label: Topic 10
toc.title: Reconstruction (1865-1896)
toc.covers: Plans for rebuilding the South, the 13th-15th Amendments, the end of Reconstruction, and the rise of Jim Crow.

toc.label: Topic 11
toc.title: The West (1858-1896)
toc.covers: Mining, railroads, ranching, and farming on the frontier and conflict with Native American nations.

toc.label: Topic 12
toc.title: New Industry and a Changing Society
toc.covers: Late-19th-century industrialisation, big business and labour, immigration and city growth, and reform in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era.

toc.label: Topic 13
toc.title: Expansion and War
toc.covers: American overseas expansion, the Spanish-American War, and U.S. involvement in World War I.

toc.label: Topic 14
toc.title: The 1920s and 1930s
toc.covers: The Roaring Twenties, the Great Depression, and the New Deal.

toc.label: Topic 15
toc.title: World War II
toc.covers: The road to war, the home front, the war in Europe and the Pacific, and the Holocaust.

toc.label: Topic 16
toc.title: The Cold War
toc.covers: Containment, the Korean War, the arms race, and postwar American society.

toc.label: Topic 17
toc.title: Civil Rights and American Society
toc.covers: The civil rights movement, the Great Society, the Vietnam era, and other movements for equal rights.

toc.label: Topic 18
toc.title: America Since the 1970s
toc.covers: Watergate, the conservative resurgence, the end of the Cold War, September 11, and recent decades.

notes: ISBN 9780079022776 is the middle-school 'Voices and Perspectives' book, not the high-school 'United States History' by the same author team, so this is a grade 6-8 text. Topic titles and date ranges come from the publisher's at-a-glance TOC; lesson titles were not found. The publisher also sells Early Years and Modern Times splits of this book. An Inquiry Journal cover mock-up in the program overview shows a different 32-topic list; the at-a-glance TOC is the one to trust. 9780079022790 is the matching Teacher Edition.
